title: An array literal at `array<float>` stores floats, an existing `array<int>` is not an `array<float>`, and `as array<float>` converts one into a new array
scope:
How an `int` or `uint` meets a `float` element of an array: in an array literal, in an array that
already exists, and in `as array<float>`. The shape half is [0236](0236.md).
dependsOnText:
[0007](0007.md) and [0054](0054.md) (the `int` → `float` widening is the one implicit
conversion), [0236](0236.md) (an existing value's `int` field does not satisfy a `float` one).

summary.headline: Whole numbers in a float array
summary.body:
`array<float> $a = [1, 2];` stores `1.0` and `2.0`, and so does `[$count]` with an `int` variable.
An `array<int>` you already have is not an `array<float>`: passing, returning or assigning one there
does not compile. `$counts as array<float>` converts it. The result is a new array of floats, and
the conversion throws for a whole number above 2^53.
